hints: Focus on where sodium and sulfur sit in Period 3 and how nuclear charge changes across a period.
Sodium is in Group 1 on the left and sulfur is in Group 16 on the right, so think about which atomic radius is larger.
Now think about the ions in Na2S, Na+ loses its outer shell while S2- keeps all three shells and gains repulsion, so decide which ion ends up larger.
walkthrough:
**Compare the atomic radii**

Both sodium and sulfur are in Period 3, so they both have electrons in three shells. Across the period from Na to S, proton number increases from 11 to 16.

Trend rule:
$$\text{greater nuclear charge across a period} \rightarrow \text{stronger pull} \rightarrow \text{smaller atomic radius}$$

**Decide which atom is bigger**

Sodium has less nuclear charge pulling on the same number of shells, so its outer electron is held less tightly. Sulfur has many more protons pulling the same shells in closer.

Conclusion:
$$\text{atomic radius: Na} > \text{S}$$

**Compare the ionic radii**

In $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$ the ions are $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{S}^{2-}$. Sodium loses its $n=3$ electron:
$$\text{Na } (2,8,1) \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ (2,8) + e^-$$
Sulfur gains two electrons but keeps its three shells:
$$\text{S } (2,8,6) + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{S}^{2-} (2,8,8)$$
Losing a whole shell makes $\text{Na}^+$ very small, while extra electron repulsion makes $\text{S}^{2-}$ larger than its atom.

**Put it together**

Atomic radius is greater for sodium, but ionic radius is greater for sulfur (as sulfide). That matches sodium is greater for atomic radius and sulfur is greater for ionic radius.

options.A: Incorrect. It reverses both trends. Atomic radius decreases across Period 3, so sulfur cannot be larger than sodium, and Na+ is much smaller than S2- because it has lost a shell.
options.B: Incorrect. The ionic part is right because S2- is larger than Na+, but the atomic part is wrong. Sulfur has higher nuclear charge than sodium in the same period, so its atom is smaller, not larger.
options.C: Incorrect. The atomic part is right because Na is larger than S, but the ionic part is wrong. Students choosing this forget that Na+ loses its outer shell and shrinks dramatically, while S2- expands.
options.D: Correct. Atomic radius: Na > S due to decreasing radius across Period 3 with increasing nuclear charge. Ionic radius: S2- > Na+ because Na+ loses the n=3 shell (2,8) while S2- retains three shells with increased repulsion (2,8,8).
